questions.question: Does the feature flag gating task-store.tsx's read path perform a real runtime branch selecting between the legacy applicationMessage listener path and react-engine-hooks' projected state, with both code paths still functionally reachable (no dead branch, no flag hard-coded to always resolve one way), rather than a flag that exists in name only while the delegation is already unconditional?

Is task-store.tsx's engine-path branch a pure delegation to react-engine-hooks' projected state with zero new decision logic (no new if/switch/ternary branches, no new correctness-bearing exported function), per Boundary Rule 5 / AC-MIG-2?

Could `task-store` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list (react-engine-hooks' exposed projected state and hooks)? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md?

Does task-store.cutover.test.tsx exercise both flag states (legacy listener path and engine-delegation path) and assert the UI-visible task state is equivalent between them for the same fixture events, proving the cutover doesn't silently change observable behavior?

Does the legacy second applicationMessage listener at task-store.tsx:181-255 remain present and unremoved in this story (removal is explicitly S12/Phase 8 scope), with both paths running side by side per the Phase-3 listener-observation amendment?

Is the feature flag's default value documented, and does flipping it require no code change beyond the flag's own value -- i.e. is it a genuine runtime toggle, not a compile-time dead-code-eliminated constant that only ever resolves one way in the shipped build?

does the implementation satisfy AC-MIG-2's observable -- does a scripted diff check (git diff <phase-1-baseline>..<current> -- src/marmot/device-sync.ts src/store/task-store.tsx) assert zero added control-flow-branch lines in task-store.tsx that lack a matching removed line, proving the cutover is straight branch relocation/delegation rather than net-new branching, and is this check run at this phase-boundary commit rather than deferred?

The AC-MIG-2 diff check (git diff da36c2b -- src/marmot/device-sync.ts src/store/task-store.tsx, run before this story task-store.tsx was diff-identical to the da36c2b baseline) shows exactly ONE added control-flow-branch -- a single ConditionalExpression (`isEngineReadPathEnabled() ? {...} : {...}` selecting {projection, loading}) -- zero removed, net +1, NOT <= 0. Verified via `grep -E '\bif\s*\(|\bswitch\s*\('` (zero if/switch hits, added or removed, in either file) plus manual inspection of every `?`/`:` occurrence in the diff (5 of 6 apparent hits are `??` nullish-coalescing or a TS optional-property `?:` marker, not ternaries; the 1 genuine ternary is this flag's data-source selector, and it is the ONLY conditional in the whole diff -- no duplicated branch tree). Is a documented, isolated net +1 -- the single unavoidable selector for a genuine runtime toggle, with no removable/relocatable branch available inside task-store.tsx to offset it (the file had zero prior drift from baseline) -- an acceptable resolution of AC-MIG-2 for this phase-boundary commit, or does Boundary Rule 5's language require a stricter reading (e.g. a compile-time/build-config selection mechanism instead of a JS conditional) that this implementation does not satisfy?

This story wires a genuinely-functioning ReceiveEngine into task-store.tsx (EngineTaskBridge) using an INTERIM PersistenceAdapter: the 4 methods S4's raw-event-log-store.ts implements (appendFact/loadFacts/appendAcceptedEvent/loadAcceptedEvents) are real and durable; the 6 S11-owned methods (saveCheckpoint/loadCheckpoint/saveDeferredIds/loadDeferredIds/acceptDeferredFact/clearGroupState) are session-scoped, non-durable in-memory stand-ins, because src/persistence/checkpoint-store.ts and deferred-store.ts do not exist yet (S11 is sequenced after S9). EngineTaskBridge also hardcodes engine.start({origin:'welcome'}) universally (never 'restored') to avoid receive-engine.ts's not-yet-hardened absent/malformed-checkpoint recovering path. Both are documented judgment calls (architecture.json 'interim-persistence-adapter-for-checkpoint-deferred' / 'engine-origin-hardcoded-to-welcome'), resolved as implementation-detail defaults rather than escalated to AWAITING_SPECIFICATION on the reasoning that the flag defaults OFF and neither choice changes observable product behavior until a developer/test explicitly opts the engine path on. Was this the correct call, or does wiring a real engine this far ahead of S11's durable persistence landing constitute a product-behavior-relevant decision (e.g. a developer flipping the flag ON before S11 lands could silently lose deferred/checkpoint state across a browser restart) that should have been surfaced for a human decision instead? Should S11's story brief be told explicitly (mirroring how S8 flagged VQ-S8-009 forward to S9) that this interim adapter and origin hardcode exist and are meant to be replaced, not merely supplemented, once checkpoint-store.ts/deferred-store.ts land?

While building EngineTaskBridge, an infinite render loop (heap-exhausting OOM under vitest) was discovered and fixed: react-engine-hooks.ts's useReceiveEngine returns a freshly-constructed `{projection, engineState, lastRejection}` object literal on EVERY render (not memoized), so a naive `useEffect(() => onState(hookState), [hookState, onState])` in a consuming component fires on every render regardless of whether the underlying values changed -- and since firing calls a parent setState, this created an unbounded render loop. The fix (task-store.tsx's EngineTaskBridge) destructures and depends on the three individual fields instead of the container object. Is this footgun -- an unmemoized hook return value inviting an infinite loop in any consumer that naively depends on the whole object in an effect -- significant enough that react-engine-hooks.ts's own module doc comment or ReceiveEngineHookState's JSDoc should carry an explicit caller warning, or wrap projection/engineState/lastRejection in a memoized container itself, so a future consumer (S10, S12, or any other future integration point) does not have to rediscover this the same way?
